items.q: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 염소들은 배가 고픈데 주변에 풀이 하나도 없다.
염소들은 주변에서 신선한 풀을 많이 찾았다.
Big Goat는 트롤을 무서워해서 아무 말도 하지 않는다.
items.exp: 염소들은 배가 고픈데 풀이 하나도 없어서 먹이를 찾아야 해요. 신선한 풀은 긴 다리 건너편에 있고 트롤은 다리 아래에 살아요.
items.passage:
Middle Goat: I'm so hungry.
Little Goat: Me, too. There is no grass at all.
Big Goat: We have to find some food.
Middle Goat: I know that there is a lot of fresh grass over the long bridge.
Little Goat: But ... a troll lives under that long bridge.
Middle Goat, Big Goat: A troll?
Little Goat: Yes, a scary troll. It's very big and strong. It likes eating animals.
Middle Goat: Oh, no. Then, what should we do?
Big Goat: Let's think of a plan. We can trick the troll.
Little Goat: How about this plan?

items.q: 밑줄 친 no ... at all의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: There is no grass at all.은 '풀이 전혀 없다'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Little Goat: Me, too. [There is no grass at all.]

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?

There ___ a lot of fresh grass over the long bridge.
items.exp: grass는 셀 수 없는 명사이고 현재의 일이므로 There is가 알맞아요.
items.passage: Middle Goat: I know that [there ___] a lot of fresh grass over the long bridge.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: There was some water in a bottle yesterday.
There are books in your bag.
There is many students in the room.
There were two birds on the tree.
There is a cat under the table.
items.exp: There is/are 뒤의 명사가 복수(many students)이면 are를 써야 해요.
items.passage: [There is] no grass at all.

items.q: 밑줄 친 have to와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?
items.exp: have to+동사원형은 '~해야 한다'라는 뜻으로 must와 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
items.passage: Big Goat: We [have to] find some food.

items.q: 밑줄 친 that과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
items.exp: I know that ~의 that은 목적어절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사로 생략할 수 있어요. I hope that ~의 that도 접속사이고, 나머지는 '저것, 저'의 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Middle Goat: I know [that] there is a lot of fresh grass over the long bridge.

items.q: 밑줄 친 likes eating과 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?
items.exp: like는 to부정사와 동명사를 모두 목적어로 취하므로 likes eating은 likes to eat으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
items.passage: It [likes eating] animals.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
items.exp: like는 목적어로 to부정사나 동명사를 써요. likes eat처럼 동사원형을 바로 쓸 수 없어요.
items.passage: It [likes eating] animals.

items.q: '우리가 무엇을 해야 할까?'라는 뜻이 되도록 알맞게 쓴 것은?
items.exp: 「의문사+조동사+주어+동사원형 ~?」의 어순으로 What should we do?가 돼요. 상대방에게 조언을 구하는 표현이에요.
items.passage: Middle Goat: Oh, no. Then, [what should we do?]

items.q: 밑줄 친 think of의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: think of ~는 '~을 생각해 내다, ~을 떠올리다'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Big Goat: Let's [think of] a plan. We can trick the troll.

items.q: 밑줄 친 How about this plan?과 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?
items.exp: How about ~?은 '~은 어때?'라는 뜻으로 What about ~?과 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
items.passage: Little Goat: [How about this plan?]

items.q: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 트롤은 매우 크고 힘이 세며 동물을 먹는 것을 좋아한다.
items.exp: Little Goat는 트롤이 무섭고 아주 크고 힘이 세며 동물을 잡아먹는 것을 좋아한다고 말했어요.
items.passage:
Middle Goat: I'm so hungry.
Little Goat: Me, too. There is no grass at all.
Big Goat: We have to find some food.
Middle Goat: I know that there is a lot of fresh grass over the long bridge.
Little Goat: But ... a troll lives under that long bridge.
Middle Goat, Big Goat: A troll?
Little Goat: Yes, a scary troll. It's very big and strong. It likes eating animals.
Middle Goat: Oh, no. Then, what should we do?
Big Goat: Let's think of a plan. We can trick the troll.
Little Goat: How about this plan?

items.q: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Little Goat는 다리를 건너고 싶지 않다.
Little Goat는 배 밑에 북을 숨기고 가장 먼저 다리를 건너려 한다.
items.exp: Little Goat는 I will go first.라고 말하고 배 밑에 북을 숨겼어요.
items.passage:
Little Goat: OK, then I will go first.
(Little Goat hides a drum under his belly.)
Troll: Hey, you! Where are you going?
Little Goat: Oh, dear! I'm looking for some food. I want to eat the grass over there.
Troll: You cannot cross the bridge. I'm going to eat you!

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
items.exp: 의문사가 있는 현재진행형 의문문은 「의문사+be동사+주어+동사원형-ing ~?」의 어순이에요. Where are you going?이 알맞아요.
items.passage: Troll: Hey, you! [Where are you going?]

items.q: 밑줄 친 looking for의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: look for ~는 '~을 찾다'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Little Goat: I'm [looking for] some food.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: I want to eat the grass.
I need to cross the bridge.
items.exp: want는 to부정사를 목적어로 취해요. want eat이 아니라 want to eat이 되어야 해요.
items.passage: Little Goat: I [want to eat] the grass over there.

items.q: 밑줄 친 cannot cross와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?
items.exp: cannot은 can't와 같은 뜻으로 '~할 수 없다'를 나타내요.
items.passage: Troll: You [cannot cross] the bridge.

items.q: 밑줄 친 I'm going to eat you!와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?
items.exp: be going to+동사원형은 '~할 것이다'라는 뜻으로 will+동사원형과 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
items.passage: Troll: You cannot cross the bridge. [I'm going to eat you!]

items.q: 밑줄 친 Don't eat me.와 같은 의미의 문장은?
items.exp: Don't+동사원형(부정명령문)은 '~하지 마라'라는 뜻이에요. 강조할 때는 Don't 대신 Never를 쓸 수도 있어요.
items.passage: Little Goat: [Don't eat me.] I'm so small.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?

You ___ be full.
items.exp: won't는 will not의 줄임말로 '~하지 않을 것이다'라는 뜻이에요. 조동사 뒤에는 동사원형 be가 와요.
items.passage: Little Goat: I'm so small. You [___] be full.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?

Wait ___ the next goat.
items.exp: '~을 기다리다'는 wait for ~로 써요.
items.passage: Little Goat: [Wait ___] the next goat.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?

She is ___ than me!
items.exp: 비교급 문장이고 big은 짧은 단어이므로 -er을 붙여 bigger가 돼요. 마지막 자음을 한 번 더 써야 해요.
items.passage: Little Goat: Another goat will come after me. She is [___] than me!

items.q: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Little Goat는 더 큰 염소를 기다리라고 트롤에게 말하고, 트롤은 동의한다.
트롤은 더 작은 염소를 기다리겠다고 한다.
Little Goat는 다리를 건너기 전에 북을 버린다.
items.exp: Little Goat는 다음에 더 큰 염소가 올 거라고 말했고 트롤은 OK, then.이라고 하며 Little Goat를 보내 주었어요.
items.passage:
Little Goat: Don't eat me. I'm so small. You won't be full.
Troll: I'm so hungry. I want to eat you!
Little Goat: Wait for the next goat. Another goat will come after me. She is bigger than me!
Troll: A bigger goat? Hmm ... OK, then.
(Little Goat crosses the bridge.)

items.q: 밑줄 친 말의 의도로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: You can do it.은 '너는 할 수 있어'라는 뜻으로 상대방을 격려하고 응원할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
items.passage: Big Goat: Now, it's your turn. [You can do it.]

items.q: 밑줄 친 I'll make it.의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: make it은 '해내다, 성공하다'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Middle Goat: Don't worry. [I'll make it.]

items.q:
밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 to부정사 용법이 바르게 짝지어진 것은?

I need (A) to cross the bridge (B) to eat the grass.
items.exp: (A)는 need의 목적어이므로 명사적 용법, (B)는 '풀을 먹기 위해서'라는 목적을 나타내므로 부사적 용법이에요.
items.passage: Middle Goat: Smart Troll, I need [to cross] the bridge [to eat] the grass.

items.q: 밑줄 친 No way!의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: No way!는 강하게 거절하거나 부정할 때 쓰는 표현으로 '절대 안 돼!'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Troll: [No way!] I have to eat you!

items.q: 밑줄 친 cannot wait anymore와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?
items.exp: not ~ anymore는 '더 이상 ~않다'라는 뜻으로 not ~ any longer와 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
items.passage: Troll: I [cannot wait anymore]!

items.q: 밑줄 친 like와 같은 의미로 쓰인 것은?
items.exp: 본문의 like는 '~처럼'이라는 뜻의 전치사예요. She looks like her mother의 like도 '~처럼, ~을 닮은'이라는 뜻이고, 나머지는 '좋아하다'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Middle Goat: You'll become stupid [like] me.

items.q: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 트롤은 Middle Goat에게 문제를 냈고, Middle Goat는 모른다고 대답했다.
트롤은 Middle Goat를 바로 보내 주었다.
items.exp: 트롤이 2 더하기 1이 얼마냐고 묻자 Middle Goat는 I don't know.라고 대답했고, 트롤은 어리석다며 웃었어요.
items.passage:
Big Goat: Now, it's your turn. You can do it.
Middle Goat: Don't worry. I'll make it.
(Middle Goat hides a drum under her belly.)
Troll: Hey, you!
Middle Goat: Smart Troll, I need to cross the bridge to eat the grass.
Troll: No way! I have to eat you! I cannot wait anymore!
Middle Goat: Don't eat me. I'm stupid. You'll become stupid like me.
Troll: Really? Then, I will ask you a question. What is two plus one?
Middle Goat: That is ... uh ... I don't know.
Troll: What a stupid goat! Ha, ha, ha, ha! Two plus one is five.
Middle Goat: Wait for the next goat. He is smarter than me! Also, he is the biggest goat in our town.
Troll: Hmm ... I don't want to be stupid like you. And the biggest goat ... OK! I will wait.

items.q: 우리말에 맞게 감탄문을 쓴 것은? (정말 영리한 염소로구나!)
items.exp: What 감탄문은 「What a/an+형용사+명사 (+주어+동사)!」의 형태예요.
items.passage: Troll: [What a stupid goat!]

items.q:
다음 문장을 감탄문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?

She is a very pretty girl.
choices: How a pretty girl she is!
What a pretty girl she is!
What a pretty she is girl!
items.exp: 명사(a pretty girl)를 강조할 때는 What 감탄문을 쓰고, 어순은 What a+형용사+명사+주어+동사예요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 문장을 3형식으로 바꿔 쓴 것은?
choices: I will ask a question of you.
I will ask a question at you.
I will ask a question for you.
I will ask you of a question.
I will ask of a question you.
items.exp: 수여동사 ask가 쓰인 4형식 문장은 「ask+직접목적어+of+간접목적어」로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
items.passage: Troll: Then, [I will ask you a question.]

items.q:
(A), (B)에 알맞은 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것은?

He is (A) than me. He is the (B) goat in our town.
items.exp: than이 있으므로 (A)는 비교급 smarter, 「the+최상급+in+장소」이므로 (B)는 최상급 biggest예요.
items.passage: Middle Goat: He is [smarter than] me! Also, he is [the biggest goat in] our town.

items.q: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 트롤은 가장 큰 염소가 싫어서 도망간다.
트롤은 어리석어지고 싶지 않아서 가장 큰 염소를 기다리기로 한다.
items.exp: 트롤은 I don't want to be stupid like you.라고 말하고 가장 큰 염소를 기다리기로 했어요.
items.passage:
Big Goat: Now, it's your turn. You can do it.
Middle Goat: Don't worry. I'll make it.
(Middle Goat hides a drum under her belly.)
Troll: Hey, you!
Middle Goat: Smart Troll, I need to cross the bridge to eat the grass.
Troll: No way! I have to eat you! I cannot wait anymore!
Middle Goat: Don't eat me. I'm stupid. You'll become stupid like me.
Troll: Really? Then, I will ask you a question. What is two plus one?
Middle Goat: That is ... uh ... I don't know.
Troll: What a stupid goat! Ha, ha, ha, ha! Two plus one is five.
Middle Goat: Wait for the next goat. He is smarter than me! Also, he is the biggest goat in our town.
Troll: Hmm ... I don't want to be stupid like you. And the biggest goat ... OK! I will wait.

items.q: 밑줄 친 When과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: [When] I was young, I believed in Santa Claus.
items.exp: 본문의 When은 '~할 때'라는 뜻의 접속사예요. 첫 번째 보기도 접속사이고, 나머지는 '언제'라는 뜻의 의문사예요.
items.passage: [When] Big Goat comes closer, Troll looks at himself in the mirror.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?

Troll looks at ___ in the mirror.
items.exp: 주어(Troll)와 목적어가 같은 대상일 때는 재귀대명사를 써요. 남성 3인칭 단수이므로 himself가 알맞아요.
items.passage: Troll looks at [___] in the mirror.

items.q: 재귀대명사가 바르지 않은 것은?
items.exp: it의 재귀대명사는 itself예요. itselves라는 말은 없어요.
items.passage: Troll looks at [himself] in the mirror.

items.q: Troll이 거울을 보고 밑줄 친 말을 한 이유로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 거울에 비친 자신의 모습을 다른 트롤로 착각해서
items.exp: Big Goat가 가까이 오자 트롤은 거울에 비친 자기 모습을 보고 다른 트롤이라고 생각했어요.
items.passage:
(Middle Goat crosses the bridge.)
Big Goat: OK! I'm coming, Troll!
(Big Goat holds a big mirror and runs to Troll. When Big Goat comes closer, Troll looks at himself in the mirror.)
Troll: Oh, that's not a goat. That's a troll!
Big Goat: (In a scary voice) I'm hungry. I'm here to eat you!
Troll: Oh, no. A big troll is coming here to eat me!
Big Goat: You know what? There are more trolls behind you!
Troll: What?
(Troll tries to run away from Big Goat.)

items.q: 밑줄 친 to eat과 쓰임(용법)이 같은 것은?
choices: My dream is [to be] a doctor.
It is fun [to swim] in summer.
I went to the park [to ride] a bike.
items.exp: 본문의 to eat은 '~하기 위해서'라는 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법이에요. 공원에 간 목적을 나타내는 to ride가 같고, 나머지는 명사적 용법이에요.
items.passage: Big Goat: I'm here [to eat] you!

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?

You know what? There ___ more trolls behind you!
items.exp: more trolls는 복수 명사이고 현재의 일이므로 There are가 알맞아요.
items.passage: Big Goat: You know what? [There ___] more trolls behind you!

items.q: 밑줄 친 tries to run away의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: try+to부정사는 '~하려고 애쓰다, 노력하다'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Troll [tries to run away] from Big Goat.

items.q: Little Goat와 Middle Goat가 트롤 뒤에서 북을 친 이유로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 더 많은 트롤이 오는 것처럼 소리를 내려고
items.exp: Big Goat가 트롤 뒤에 더 많은 트롤이 있다고 말한 뒤, 북소리로 더 많은 트롤이 오는 것처럼 트롤을 속였어요.
items.passage:
Little Goat: (In a low voice) Let's hit the drum, now!
(Little Goat and Middle Goat hit the drums loudly behind the troll.)
Troll: Ahhhhh! What's that sound? More trolls are coming! Oh, no!
(Troll jumps into the river to run away and never comes back.)
Little Goat, Middle Goat, Big Goat: Yay! We beat the troll together!
Big Goat: Let's eat fresh grass!
(When the three goats see the fresh green grass, they all jump for joy.)

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?

More trolls ___ ! Oh, no!
items.exp: 주어 More trolls가 복수이고 지금 오고 있는 중이므로 현재진행형 are coming이 알맞아요.
items.passage: Troll: What's that sound? More trolls [___]! Oh, no!

items.q: 밑줄 친 never comes back의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: never는 '절대 ~않다'라는 뜻의 빈도부사로 일반동사 앞에 써요. never comes back은 '다시는 돌아오지 않는다'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Troll jumps into the river to run away and [never comes back].

items.q: 밑줄 친 beat와 같은 의미로 쓰인 것은?
choices: I like the beat of this song.
items.exp: 본문의 beat는 '이기다'라는 뜻이에요. 첫 번째 보기도 '이기다'라는 뜻이고, 나머지는 '(달걀을) 휘젓다', '(심장이) 뛰다', '박자', '(북을) 치다'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Yay! We [beat] the troll together!

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
items.exp: 「Let's+동사원형」은 '(우리) ~하자'라는 뜻이에요. eating이 아니라 eat이 되어야 해요.
items.passage: Big Goat: [Let's eat] fresh grass!

items.q: 밑줄 친 jump for joy의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: jump for joy는 '기뻐 날뛰다'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: they all [jump for joy].

items.q:
이야기의 흐름에 맞게 순서를 배열한 것은?

(가) Big Goat showed a mirror to Troll.
(나) Little Goat told Troll to wait for a bigger goat.
(다) Middle Goat said she was stupid and asked Troll to wait for the biggest goat.
items.exp: Little Goat가 가장 먼저 다리를 건넜고(나), 다음에 Middle Goat(다), 마지막으로 Big Goat가 거울을 이용해(가) 트롤을 속였어요.

items.q: 위 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: A Lonely Goat in the Town
The Goat Who Lost His Drum
Three Clever Goats Beat the Troll
items.exp: 세 마리 염소가 지혜를 모아 트롤을 속이고 이긴 이야기이므로 'Three Clever Goats Beat the Troll'이 알맞아요.
items.passage:
Middle Goat: I'm so hungry.
Little Goat: Me, too. There is no grass at all.
Big Goat: We have to find some food.
Middle Goat: I know that there is a lot of fresh grass over the long bridge.
Little Goat: But ... a troll lives under that long bridge.
Middle Goat, Big Goat: A troll?
Little Goat: Yes, a scary troll. It's very big and strong. It likes eating animals.
Middle Goat: Oh, no. Then, what should we do?
Big Goat: Let's think of a plan. We can trick the troll.
Little Goat: How about this plan?
Little Goat: OK, then I will go first.
(Little Goat hides a drum under his belly.)
Troll: Hey, you! Where are you going?
Little Goat: Oh, dear! I'm looking for some food. I want to eat the grass over there.
Troll: You cannot cross the bridge. I'm going to eat you!
Little Goat: Don't eat me. I'm so small. You won't be full.
Troll: I'm so hungry. I want to eat you!
Little Goat: Wait for the next goat. Another goat will come after me. She is bigger than me!
Troll: A bigger goat? Hmm ... OK, then.
(Little Goat crosses the bridge.)
Big Goat: Now, it's your turn. You can do it.
Middle Goat: Don't worry. I'll make it.
(Middle Goat hides a drum under her belly.)
Troll: Hey, you!
Middle Goat: Smart Troll, I need to cross the bridge to eat the grass.
Troll: No way! I have to eat you! I cannot wait anymore!
Middle Goat: Don't eat me. I'm stupid. You'll become stupid like me.
Troll: Really? Then, I will ask you a question. What is two plus one?
Middle Goat: That is ... uh ... I don't know.
Troll: What a stupid goat! Ha, ha, ha, ha! Two plus one is five.
Middle Goat: Wait for the next goat. He is smarter than me! Also, he is the biggest goat in our town.
Troll: Hmm ... I don't want to be stupid like you. And the biggest goat ... OK! I will wait.
(Middle Goat crosses the bridge.)
Big Goat: OK! I'm coming, Troll!
(Big Goat holds a big mirror and runs to Troll. When Big Goat comes closer, Troll looks at himself in the mirror.)
Troll: Oh, that's not a goat. That's a troll!
Big Goat: (In a scary voice) I'm hungry. I'm here to eat you!
Troll: Oh, no. A big troll is coming here to eat me!
Big Goat: You know what? There are more trolls behind you!
Troll: What?
(Troll tries to run away from Big Goat.)
Little Goat: (In a low voice) Let's hit the drum, now!
(Little Goat and Middle Goat hit the drums loudly behind the troll.)
Troll: Ahhhhh! What's that sound? More trolls are coming! Oh, no!
(Troll jumps into the river to run away and never comes back.)
Little Goat, Middle Goat, Big Goat: Yay! We beat the troll together!
Big Goat: Let's eat fresh grass!
(When the three goats see the fresh green grass, they all jump for joy.)
